name: Shemaiah
overview: Shemaiah was a male Levite known for his leadership role as the chief of the sons of Elizaphan. His position highlights his significance within the tribe of Levi, entrusted with responsibilities among the Levitical families. There are no additional notes recorded about him.
namesAndTitles: The name Shemaiah means 'YHWH hears,' reflecting a theophoric element common in Hebrew names, indicating a connection to God's attentive nature. This name is recorded in 1 Chronicles 15:8.
familyAndRelationships: Shemaiah is identified as a descendant of Elzaphan, establishing his lineage within the Levitical family. Scripture does not record any other family relationships for him beyond this connection.
scriptureSignificance: Shemaiah's significance in the biblical narrative stems from his leadership as chief of the sons of Elizaphan, a notable Levitical family. This role would have involved overseeing duties assigned to his family within the service of the tabernacle or temple. His mention in 1 Chronicles 15:8 situates him within the organization of temple worship during the time of David.
